position_vocabulary.note: Named positions first; the issue allows a small ordered scale only after playtesting, which is why 'rank' exists here as an ordering aid and not as a game quantity. Do NOT equate an ideological position with fixed personality, intelligence, morality, psychic power or predetermined loyalty, and remember that a faction's publicly advertised position can differ from its hidden agenda.

axes.label: Left vs Right (economic politics)
axes.high_pole: capitalism, private property, competitive markets, accumulation
axes.significance: Who owns and allocates resources. Not identical to attitudes toward authority.

axes.label: Liberal vs Conservative (cultural politics)
axes.low_pole: progressive, pluralist, individual freedom and changing norms
axes.high_pole: traditionalist, continuity, inherited norms and social hierarchy
axes.significance: Cultural orientation. This is NOT the conventional Political Compass authoritarian/libertarian vertical axis; if the Compass is used literally, model authoritarianism/libertarianism separately or rename this dimension. Governance positions are captured by governance tags instead.
axes.author_decision_open: whether this axis is enough or a distinct authoritarian/libertarian value is also necessary

axes.label: AGI / technological transformation
axes.significance: Overall response to rapid AGI and breakthrough technology. Nuances about BCI, robotics, cybernetics, quantum computing and transhumanism belong in specific tags: a faction may oppose autonomous AGI while strongly supporting human augmentation.

axes.label: NHI contact / integration
axes.low_pole: isolation, human exclusivism; extremes may call for eradication
axes.high_pole: acceptance, coexistence, contact and integration; extremes may become cultic submission
axes.significance: GENERAL policy toward NHI, not loyalty to a single civilization. Tolerance, collaboration, assimilation, submission and genocide are distinguished by tags, policies and goals, not by one number.

axes.label: PSI / consciousness ontology
axes.low_pole: materialism, functionalist and computational accounts, scepticism toward PSI
axes.high_pole: idealism, fundamental or cosmic consciousness, panpsychism and PSI openness
axes.significance: Metaphysical commitments and PSI policy. BELIEF IS NOT ABILITY: a QIP believer need not be an accomplished psychic, and a scientifically minded materialist may still acknowledge empirical anomalies in this fiction.

tag_kinds.label: a thing the holder owns or operates
a tie to someone or something else

tag_families.label: Consciousness and PSI doctrine
tag_families.note: BELIEF, distinct from the abilities below. A believer need not be capable, and a capable person need not believe.

tag_families.label: PSI and cognitive capability
tag_families.note: Competence, not doctrine and not equipment. These are the ids the codex's translation scene can consume as research.

tag_families.label: NHI policy and allegiances
tag_families.note: Positions and postures. These say nothing structural about the per-polity diplomatic states below, and nothing here is derived from the NHI axis.

tag_families.label: Social and governance doctrine
tag_families.note: This is where authoritarianism, democracy, anarchism and civil-liberties positions belong, so the cultural axis is not asked to carry them.

tag_families.label: Organisational capabilities
tag_families.note: One tag definition, different context: REMOTE_VIEWING_TEAM is a faction's asset and REMOTE_VIEWER is a character's competence. Same vocabulary, different scopes, and they are not interchangeable.

nhi_polities.label: Union of Collective Consciousness Communes (UCCC)
nhi_polities.note: the locked official label. The service-to-others bloc: a communist social memory complex in the Confederal register. This issue's text calls it 'Confederacy/Zookeepers'; that wording is recorded here as notation, not as the official name.

nhi_polities.label: Greater Orion Arm Co-Prosperity Sphere
nhi_polities.note: the locked official label. The service-to-self bloc: capitalist corporations with Grey, Mantid and Reptilian tendencies.

nhi_polities.label: other extraterrestrial, interdimensional, extratempestrial and cryptoterrestrial origins
nhi_polities.note: at least these exist alongside the two blocs; a diplomatic state can be held toward them individually.

separation_rule.note: Issue #346: avoid forcing pro-NHI to equal pro-Confederacy or pro-Orion. A pro-contact diplomat may oppose both hierarchies and seek relations with independent NHI, and a xenophobic hardliner may seek the extermination of both. The axis is how welcoming a faction is toward contact in general; the relations are separate, mutable ties to each named polity. Neither is derived from the other in code.

faction_creation_flow.note: simple descriptors before numbers or sliders

faction_creation_flow.label: Pick a few defining tags
faction_creation_flow.note: including one positive political goal, one taboo or red line, and one distinguishing doctrine

faction_creation_flow.label: Define NHI relationships individually
faction_creation_flow.note: where known; unknown contacts stay hidden or unrevealed

faction_creation_flow.label: Create the faction leader
faction_creation_flow.note: with their own possibly different ideology and tags; other agents and managers have individual convictions and may disagree with leadership

faction_creation_flow.label: Generate tensions

fog_of_war.note: Issue #346: a player's knowledge of actual NHI connections can differ from their public ideology, and tags and axes must not reveal classified author canon on the starting UI.
fog_of_war.public_vs_hidden: A faction's publicly advertised position can differ from its hidden agenda; both are stored, and only the public one is shown.

event_seed.label: The Neutral Laboratory
event_seed.premise: A small independent laboratory has independently documented anomalous observations. Its director offers access to a public briefing and invites the faction to help protect participants' consent and data. A private-sector sponsor separately offers equipment in exchange for an exclusive publishing window.

cast.public_position: Supports open and reproducible investigation; wary of secrecy and financial capture
Supports ambitious technology research and partnership, but asks for preferential access
Wants participant consent and meaningful public accountability

beats.prompt: The director asks how the faction would publish sensitive evidence without exposing participants. The sponsor offers immediate practical help on its own conditions.
beats.surface: Present the faction's publicly stated AGI/technology, PSI and cultural positions and relevant doctrine, goal or resource TAGs. The director's trust remains an NPC judgement, not a computed ideology score.

beats.prompt: The community organizer challenges the sponsor's exclusivity clause while a skeptical researcher asks whether PSI claims have been replicated.
beats.surface: A materialist character with REMOTE_VIEWER competence, or an anti-AGI character with HUMAN_AUGMENTATION, may argue their positions without being rejected as contradictory. Belief does not grant psychic capability.

beats.prompt: Choose a public commitment and an actionable next scene.
beats.surface: The GM checks what players actually promise, available relationships and evidence; no secret polity information is disclosed.

choices.label: Public protocol, consent first
choices.explicit_commitment: Publish a consent-based testing protocol and protect participant identities.
choices.follow_up: Negotiate with the director and organizer over independent oversight and a replication session.
choices.cost_or_tension: The sponsor may withdraw exclusive funding; an impatient supporter may criticize the delay.

choices.label: Conditional corporate partnership
choices.explicit_commitment: Accept limited equipment support only under written independence, consent and disclosure terms.
choices.follow_up: Negotiate the contract and investigate whether the conditions can be enforced.
choices.cost_or_tension: Activists may question independence; the patron may reject restrictions.

choices.label: Quiet independent verification
choices.explicit_commitment: Delay publication, preserve evidence and seek a second investigator.
choices.follow_up: Recruit an outside researcher and address the director's concern about delay and trust.
choices.cost_or_tension: Participants may fear indefinite secrecy; competitors can publish first.

event_seed.outcome_policy: No automatic success, predetermined alliance, faction morality score, fixed resource change, forced NPC recruitment or canonical NHI revelation. Resolve any follow-up through future author-approved faction rules or a GM scene. Record commitments, consent constraints, relationships and unresolved tensions as narrative state.
event_seed.nhi_separation: A welcoming NHI contact-policy position must never imply allegiance to the Confederacy or Orion. This event supplies no evidence of any named NHI polity and must not reveal hidden campaign cosmology.
event_seed.compatibility_note: Prototype for issue #346. The current code records event_seed as uninterpreted data; no new resolver, numeric modifier or faction-creation mechanic is authorized.

cautions.note: axes summarise orientations; demands, antagonisms and nodal or empty signifiers drive actual articulation and hegemonic struggle. A five-value vector is not a substitute for political discourse, contingencies or coalitions.
recruitment, movement building, contact, propaganda and communications depend on concrete networks and access.
one actor can hold different expectations in science, religion, law, politics and the economy; consider public doctrine versus internal faction practice.
use broad affinity and tension cues for recruitment and diplomacy, but never make tag combinations predetermined alliance, hatred, morality or voting behaviour.
one faction card (five positions plus a handful of tags) plus the existing character cards; avoid complex population models and avoid adding more sliders for every subgroup.
